formalDefinition: Given a directed graph G = (V, E), find all maximal subsets C of V such that for every pair of vertices u and v in C, there is a directed path from u to v and from v to u.
problemDefinition: A strongly connected component is a maximal group of vertices in a directed graph where every vertex can reach every other vertex in the same group. The goal is to return all such components.
outputDescription: The strongly connected components of G, i.e. the partition of its vertices into maximal mutually-reachable groups
source: Swati Dhingra, Poorvi S. Dodwad, and Meghna Madan, "Finding Strongly Connected Components in a Social Network Graph," International Journal of Computer Applications, Volume 136, No. 7, February 2016.
certificateFormat: Format: {c1,...,cM} | one set per strongly connected component, order does not matter Example: {{1,2,3},{4,5}}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: Finds strongly connected components in a directed graph using two depth-first searches: one on the original graph and one on the reversed graph.
defaultSolver.source: Swati Dhingra, Poorvi S. Dodwad, and Meghna Madan, "Finding Strongly Connected Components in a Social Network Graph," International Journal of Computer Applications, Volume 136, No. 7, February 2016. Section 4.4 describes Kosaraju's algorithm.

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: Verifies an SCC certificate by comparing components as unordered sets, since SCC ordering is not unique.
defaultVerifier.source: Swati Dhingra, Poorvi S. Dodwad, and Meghna Madan, "Finding Strongly Connected Components in a Social Network Graph," International Journal of Computer Applications, Volume 136, No. 7, February 2016.
